newsitem.title: UK: N. Sea Norwegians firm, Brent easier, Med sours sof.
newsitem.headline: N. Sea Norwegians firm, Brent easier, Med sours sof.

text.p: Firmer values for Norwegian grades brightened an oversupplied North Sea wet market on Wednesday but traders questioned whether early April demand was enough to haul spot crudes decisively out of the doldrums.
"The end-user buying spree that we've seen for late March makes things feel more positive," one said.
"But the question remains whether end-March buying is going to end up merely displacing early April demand."
A Forties loading April 1-3 changed hands slightly firmer at a seven cent premium to Dated Brent.
But a wet Brent loading March 26-28 was sold at April Brent -90 cents, a shade lower than Tuesday's May-related deals.
Traders said attention remained focussed on one European major holding four April Brents, saying these probably held the key to the direction of Brent in early April.
Ekofisk loading April 7-9 was done at Dated Brent +15 cents, while another loading April 9-11 traded at an eight cent premium. The grade traded at a five cent discount to Dated on Tuesday.
An April 1-3 Gullfaks C changed hands at a 10 cent premium to Dated, two cents higher than Tuesday's March 29-31 loader.
An Oseberg loading April 3-5 was done at a 10 cent premium to Dated after discounts of two and 10 cents on Tuesday.
Brent paper was around unchanged in quiet discussion. CFDs were slightly weaker at May -42 cents for next week, with the week after at around -32 cents.
Intermonths were steady at around +20 cents for April/May.

West African crude continued its tentative recovery from March lows as sales of April barrels gathered pace, traders said. A first decade Escravos was heard sold into Portugal at a small premium to Dated Brent, while a Brass River was placed into Rotterdam.
